overview:
California's 27th District leans Democratic by six points, and first-term incumbent George Whitesides enters the general election with a decisive financial edge. He has raised about $4.4 million and holds $2.3 million on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised roughly $414,000 with about $60,000 available. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Whitesides and almost nothing against him.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 96 percent. With the incumbent running in a district that favors his party and a large resource gap, the seat rates as safely Democratic, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
